Energy And The Jensen Tail Risk

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 16 Nov 2026

We never tire of pointing out that energy stocks have outperformed all other sectors in the MSCI World and S&P 500 indexes over the past five years. However, the past few weeks have seen a notable pullback in both the oil price (down roughly -20% from its pre-midterm highs) and in energy stocks. Behind this pullback in energy prices lie the greatly reduced odds of a renewed Iran war (see As The Clouds Part, Markets Anticipate End Of Iran War), the growing hopes that a truce might soon see the light of day in Ukraine (see Shudders In The Tech Complex and One Thing After Another) and even that this week’s Apec meeting in Shenzhen would be the setting for a “new Yalta”: a tripartite meeting where Russia, China and the US would settle their differences, bury hatchets, and set the stage for a new era of world peace and brotherhood amongst men of goodwill (preferably in time for the Christmas season).
